summary: Unit-tested tools/dispatch_verify.py (1,362 lines, 35 functions, the fleet's only gate between 'worker exited 0' and 'the work happened'). Half A: all 35 functions censused top-down — every one has at least one production reach path; ZERO deletion candidates. Half B: 172 tests written first and run; 170 green, 2 RED (recorded defects with owner: the empty-deliverables= arm returns PASS where the brief's SHOULD is 'unverifiable, never pass'). The module needed NO cleanup edits — its behavior matched its documented intent on every arm tested except the two named recorded defects. Tests are stdlib-only, hermetic (tempfile), clean under tests/unit/run.py.

half_a_conclusion: Zero deletion candidates. All 35 functions have at least one production reach path: 7 called directly by bin/subagent (generate_nonce, nonce_prompt_lines, parse_deliverables, verify_dispatch, record_perf, heal_dispatch + the HEAL_OWNER constant), 4 by regression scripts directly (recommended_wall, classify_task_type, wall_advisory, read_run_record), the rest internal to an externally-reachable entry (verify_dispatch / heal_dispatch / record_perf / main). The weakest four (run_census, census_classify, _trailer_classify, scan_findings) are reachable only via the manual --census / --dry-run CLI report — watch items, not deletions: they are the T630 historical-census machinery and the T488 acceptance gate, used on 2026-08-23. _deepseek_refusal_reason is a registered no-op that must stay: the T630 design's one-detector-per-family invariant requires a deepseek entry.

half_b.method: tests written first, run, colour recorded, then cleanup. First full run: 2 expected-failures (the recorded defect) + 8 test-authoring issues (all on the test side: mock return_value semantics, argv[0] handling in main, substring direction for truncated nonce, summary wording for unknown verdicts). After fixing the test bugs: 172 tests, 170 green, 2 RED recorded defects.
half_b.module_cleanup_note: The module needed NO cleanup edits: on every arm tested except the two named recorded defects, current behaviour matched the SHOULD stated in the module's own docstrings and the T411/T477/T488/T513/T520/T538/T625/T629/T630/T631 briefs. Half B's cleanup step was therefore a no-op — the honest outcome is the two recorded defects below, not a code change.
half_b.graded_vocabulary: A dedicated test pins every fail perf's fail_check to {nonce, deliverables, findings} ∪ {row, exit} — the exact set tools/model-profiles.py grades recoverable (1) vs unrecoverable (0) (RECOVERABLE_FAIL, model-profiles.py:263-268). A novel fail_check value would silently grade as unrecoverable and corrupt the close-discipline dimension; the test guards the boundary between the two instruments.

recorded_defects.owner: T793 (the brief that states the SHOULD)
recorded_defects.should: a T-id row closed as success with NO deliverables declared reports UNVERIFIABLE, never PASS — the deliverables arm silently disables itself when the declaration is empty, and a PASS resting on the nonce alone is exactly the self-report the module refuses to trust
recorded_defects.current: verify_dispatch returns exit 0 'worker reported success; side effects verified — verification PASSED' with perf verified=pass when deliverables=[] (or None) on a done+success row; the ledger records verified=pass, which model-profiles grades 2 (clean close)
recorded_defects.fix_notes: Deferred deliberately. A correct fix changes the pinned verifier's pass/fail contract (bin/subagent imports git show HEAD:tools/dispatch_verify.py, T631) and collides with tools/regression-runner-brief-telemetry.sh arm E, which passes deliverables=[] and asserts the wall-low detail on the PASS path. It needs its own row with a regression arm, a decision on the bare-file path (whose documented contract is 'the nonce is the whole guard'), and — if a new fail_check/verified value is introduced — a corresponding model-profiles RECOVERABLE_FAIL decision. The tests pin the SHOULD so that row has a red test to make green.
recorded_defects.fleet_evidence: 69 in-tree bundles declare an explicit empty deliverables= (race-b minimal/orient bundles, T227 regtest bundles) — the shape is live, not theoretical

recorded_defects.owner: T793 (same SHOULD, None is the signature default and behaves identically to [])
recorded_defects.should: deliverables=None (the signature default) must behave like [] — same silent disable, same UNVERIFIABLE requirement
recorded_defects.current: identical to the empty-list case: PASS with verified=pass
recorded_defects.fix_notes: same fix as above; the two arms guard the two spellings a caller can produce

verdict_classification: The brief's focus 4 (recoverable nonce/deliverables/findings vs unrecoverable row/exit) is implemented and now pinned: fail_check values produced by verify_dispatch across every failing arm are exactly {nonce, deliverables, findings, row, exit}, matching model-profiles RECOVERABLE_FAIL ∪ {row, exit}. No error found in the mapping.
nonce_arm: Tested present (PASS), absent (FAIL fail=nonce), mangled (mutated hex char: FAIL fail=nonce), truncated (half the token: FAIL fail=nonce — `nonce in stdout` demands the full 128-bit token), and echoed-in-a-quoted-brief (PASS: a worker that pastes the whole brief into a fenced quote demonstrably READ the prompt; the deliverables arm is what catches a read-but-did-nothing worker). The 2026-08-23 oxalpha double-catch is the live proof of the arm's value.
kanban_arm: Tested in_progress + rc=0 (kimi: FAIL fail=row), in_progress + rc!=0 (FAIL fail=row), dispatchable + rc=0 (FAIL fail=row), row-not-found (FAIL fail=row), done + rc!=0 (FAIL fail=exit). The arm fails on an open row whatever the exit code, as the brief requires.
deliverables_arm: Tested missing (FAIL fail=deliverables), present (PASS), fail-found+missing (FAIL — deliverables are hard for fail-found too), blocked/abandoned+missing (PASS with the 'deliverables absent (expected for <verdict>)' NOTE), malformed findings deliverable (FAIL fail=findings, T488), findings-parse only under findings/ (a docs/ file with garbage content passes), missing-beats-malformed (fail=deliverables), absolute paths. The git-committed half of the SHOULD is enforced upstream by the managent done gate (src/managent/main.zig deliverableVerdict, T278: tracked-and-clean / SHA256SUMS-pinned / deleted-in-history); verify_dispatch is the filesystem second line, so no git check was added here.
notes: Interference observed, not mine: while this row ran, another lane (T792) added tests/unit/test_subagent.py to the tree (untracked, 54 tests, 4 failures in TestFlagManualHeal / TestLoadPinnedDispatchVerify / TestPiSessionPath). I did not touch it — the convention is one file per lane. tests/unit/run.py therefore shows 4 failures until T792 resolves its file; my file alone (172 tests) and the token-capture file are clean. No directives were received (inbox polled at each checkpoint; 0 acked). No audited_by: this file proposes no claim-status changes, so claimlint C11 does not require an auditor.
